This work will be part of the European STAGE project, titled “An Integrated Life-Course Approach for Person-Centered Solutions and Care for Older Adults with Multimorbidity in European Regions.” Specifically, various approaches to causal inference will be applied to a case study involving repeated measurements of DNA methylation in blood or saliva, and the assessment of various outcomes to derive a multimorbidity index. The data will come from European birth cohorts, including the Italian NINFEA cohort.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Spatial statistical methods for investigating the health effects of environmental and climatic exposures (Univ. TORINO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-11 13:00
Institution: Univ. TORINO, Turin
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-24 Statistica medica, igiene generale e applicata e scienze infermieristiche generali, cliniche, pediatriche e ostetrico-ginecologiche e neonatali

The project aims to develop and apply spatial statistical methods to investigate the relationships between environmental and climatic exposures and the risk of acute and chronic diseases and, where possible, to estimate causal effects. The methodological framework will include geostatistical models, models for areal data and point process models. The analyses will focus on exposures to extreme temperatures and precipitation, drought, wildfire smoke and air pollutants (ozone, PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NO₂ and NOₓ). Health outcomes will include cancer, cardiometabolic and respiratory diseases across the life course, as well as all-cause and cause-specific mortality.

The Early Stage Researcher will be actively involved in investigating the endothelial-modulating potential of extracellular vesicles derived from colorectal cancer specimens and cell lines (CRC-EVs), using both in vitro and in vivo approaches, as well as in assessing the effects of their pharmacological modulation. In particular, the researcher will investigate in vitro the effects of colchicine and its derivatives on the intracellular fate of CRC-EVs and on the molecular pathways underlying their biological activity. item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-01 14:00

Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-02 Patologia generale e patologia clinica

B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas (B-NHL), including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and Burkitt lymphoma (BL), are aggressive malignancies frequently driven by c-MYC. Despite current therapies, relapse remains common, highlighting the need for novel strategies. Our data indicate that FGF/FGFR signaling stabilizes c-MYC and that its inhibition induces c-MYC proteasomal degradation. We hypothesize that FGF/FGFR blockade may impair c-MYC-driven B-NHL growth and dissemination. Using FGF trapping and FGFR inhibitors, we will investigate the biological and molecular effects of FGF/FGFR blockade in DLBCL and BL in vitro and in vivo, assess its therapeutic efficacy alone or combined with R-CHOP,…

Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM) are rare autoimmune disorders in which malignancy represents a major cause of morbidity and mortality, particularly in cancer-associated myositis (CAM). Up to 25% of patients with IIM are diagnosed with cancer within three years before or after myositis onset. Anti-TIF1γ antibodies, detected in 7 -31% of adults with dermatomyositis, are among the strongest predictors of cancer risk. However, 25 -50% of anti-TIF1γ-positive patients do not develop cancer. Recent evidence suggests that additional autoantibodies may modulate this risk. In particular, anti-CCAR1 antibodies have been associated with reduced cancer risk and longer latency to cancer…
